clue.text: Idle cop somehow to turn back his support?

definitions.note: the cop's support: the animal that works alongside a policeman

indicators.note: done somehow, in no fixed way, so the letters of idle cop are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for a turn from right to left

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game: whose go is it?

explanation.surface: A lazy policeman is told to turn around and fetch whatever props him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' points back to the cop of the surface, so the definition only makes sense once the cop is known to be a policeman; 'go' as a turn is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained canine partner assists an officer on patrol, so it is literally the officer's backup.

clue.text: Questions accessories needed for ballet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pump someone is to question them persistently for information
second meaning: light soft shoes, as in ballet slippers

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense, interrogating someone, sits beside a noun sense for dancers' footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Interrogating someone for facts is pumping them, and soft flat dance shoes are also called by this word.

clue.text: Allow story about Conservative? Breaking news carrying no weight

indicators.note: the story goes around the letter for Conservative

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: breaking breaks up the letters that remain so they are rearranged
carrying no weight tells us the word news must shed the abbreviation for weight

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician permits a tale about a Tory, and the breaking story turns out to be lightweight.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the American spelling of the verb; the British verb is also spelt this way, the -ce form being the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant official permission for something is to license it, a direct synonym of permit.

clue.text: Hopefully learning many are involved in this legal matter

definitions.text: Hopefully learning many are involved in this
definitions.meaning: reads as a school lesson where a roomful of pupils are taught together
a lawsuit brought on behalf of a whole group of claimants

explanation.surface: A teacher hopes a whole roomful of pupils are taking part in learning something about law.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half pictures a school group having a lesson; the phrase actually names a lawsuit brought jointly by many plaintiffs.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit filed by representatives for a large group of people with the same grievance is this kind of lawsuit.

clue.text: Everybody in staff raised money

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters run upwards, read in reverse
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Every employee pitched in and the staff collected some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The American currency unit is a kind of money, so this is a specific example of the general term.

clue.text: Old relative was not happy about rising extravagance

parts.note: gran is grandmother, an elderly relative

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: rued means regretted, was unhappy about

explanation.surface: Grandma grumbled about rising prices and lavish spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is magnificence or splendour, which an extravagant display shows off.

clue.text: First degree thus fundamental

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a first university degree
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as written

explanation.surface: A bachelor's degree is described as the essential starting point.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means essential or elementary, the bedrock on which something else rests.

clue.text: Fashion accessory obtained out of South American city

indicators.note: out of means the word for obtained is taken from the city name

parts.note: Bogota is the capital of Colombia
got means obtained

explanation.surface: Someone bought a fashion item in a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtained out of' reads as buying from, but the word got is removed from the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a long feathery scarf worn round the neck as a stylish addition to an outfit.

clue.text: Visit with estate agent, perhaps, getting invitation to check next option?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to inspect a property being shown
second meaning: the note telling a reader to look at the following page

explanation.walkthrough: Prospective buyers view a house this way; the same words also appear at the foot of a page directing the reader onward.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspecting a house for sale is to look around it, and a printed direction to turn the page uses the same phrase.

clue.text: A city rent is ridiculous? Sure thing

indicators.note: the letters of a city rent are jumbled into an absurd new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: City rents are absurdly high, and that is beyond doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is bound to happen is a dead cert, a guaranteed outcome.

clue.text: Bloke needing microphone repair after change of heart

parts.note: mic is the usual short form of microphone

indicators.note: the two central letters of the word for repair change places

parts.note: to heal is to mend or repair

explanation.surface: A man's broken microphone needs fixing once he has changed his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the heart of the word for repair changes: its middle letters swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition stands for any man's name; a bloke is a man and this is one example of a male forename.

clue.text: Inexpert fellow invested in gold? Heading for ruin

indicators.note: the fellow is placed inside the symbol for gold, as money is invested

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a mate is a companion or fellow

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unskilled investor put money into gold and is on the way to financial ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur's work is unprofessional and unskilled, so the adjective means lacking expertise.

clue.text: Boy lied? Not good

indicators.note: not good means the letter for good is left out

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song, here disguised as the past tense of lie

explanation.surface: A child has been fibbing, which is not good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lied' looks like a verb about fibbing, but it is the German word for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, so in relation to his parents he is their boy.

clue.text: Study sounds of birds avoiding northern part of Europe

parts.note: to scan is to examine closely
din is loud noise

indicators.note: avoiding means the letter for northern is left out

parts.note: avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher studies birdsong but avoids the north of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northern' looks like a geographical pointer for the region but is just the abbreviation N being removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandinavia is the northern European region of Norway, Sweden and Denmark.

clue.text: Who's got ready to study?

definitions.meaning: reads as asking who is prepared, but ready is slang for cash, as in readies
a person who studies something: here, coins and money

explanation.surface: A teacher asks which pupil is prepared to begin studying.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready, or the readies, is British slang for money, so the clue asks who has cash to study, a coin collector.
explanation.definitionFit: A numismatist is a scholar or collector of coins and currency, someone whose subject is money itself.

clue.text: Business information in current year

indicators.note: the information is placed in the abbreviation for current

parts.note: AC is alternating current
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A company's data is up to date for this year.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a firm or organisation providing a service, such as a travel or advertising company.

clue.text: Self-evident Times article turned up with peculiar expressions I'd ignored

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: ignored means the letters of I'd are left out

parts.note: idiomatic describes expressions peculiar to a language
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Times newspaper article appeared full of odd phrases that were overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a truth accepted without proof, so axiomatic means obviously true.

clue.text: Test offered by sequence in exposed cards?

parts.note: in bridge the dummy is the hand laid face up on the table
a run is a sequence, as of cards or wins

explanation.surface: A card player tests a sequence in the face-up hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, declarer's partner's hand is laid face up and is called the dummy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or trial before the real event is a practice run, so this is a test.

clue.text: Me, I will participate in most of opportunity to get fitter?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter I joins in, going inside the shortened word
most of drops the final letter of the word for opportunity

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers for a keep-fit opportunity, hoping to get into better shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitter' reads as more fit, but it is the noun for a person who fits machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitter assembles and repairs machinery, the same trade as a mechanic who services engines.

clue.text: Imaginative architectural feature in mind — millions expended

indicators.note: the architectural feature sits inside what remains of mind
expended means spent and gone, so the abbreviation for millions is used up and dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a spire is a tall tapering church tower top

explanation.surface: An architect has a grand spire in mind but millions have already been spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspired work shows brilliant creative imagination, as if prompted by genius.

clue.text: Lithium company beset by wrong element

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the wrong goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A lithium firm is accused of wrongdoing over a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'element' sits naturally beside lithium, inviting a search among metals, but the answer is the semiconductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicon is a chemical element, atomic number 14, used in microchips.

clue.text: Wrong answer — subsequently repeated in second test

indicators.note: the repeated letter goes inside the word for test

parts.note: to try is to test
the answer abbreviation A is used again

explanation.surface: An exam candidate gets the answer wrong and then again in a second test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' supplies a second A, the same abbreviation for answer used once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To go astray is to go wrong, off the correct path.

clue.text: Seek new skill? Picked up skill, staying in control

indicators.note: staying in puts the upturned skill inside the word for control

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in keeping a tight rein

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means lifted, the letters read upwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A worker learned a new trade while keeping a tight grip on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests heard or learned, but in this down clue it lifts the word, reversing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to learn new abilities, especially for a different job.

clue.text: A lot of effort to get a new advertising feature

parts.note: a slog is hard sustained work
taken as written

explanation.surface: It takes great effort to come up with fresh material for an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a catchy phrase used in marketing campaigns, a standard part of an advert.

clue.text: Nothing blocks machine, all wrecked, attaining the dumps

indicators.note: the zero for nothing blocks up the middle of the rearranged letters
wrecked means the letters of machine and all are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A jammed machine has been completely wrecked, leaving its owner deeply fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down in the dumps is being gloomy, and melancholia is a state of deep sadness.

clue.text: Bill almost crazy to return

indicators.note: to return means the shortened word goes back the other way
almost drops the last letter

parts.note: bats is slang for mad, crazy

explanation.surface: A diner says the bill was nearly crazy enough to send back.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab is a bill or account, as in picking up the tab in a bar.

clue.text: Military accessory at work, requiring billions invested

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, as if clothed in

parts.note: busy means occupied or at work

explanation.surface: A defence contractor busy on equipment needs billions put in.
explanation.walkthrough: A busby is the tall fur hat worn by some British guardsmen and hussars.
explanation.definitionFit: A busby is a tall fur ceremonial hat, an item of military headwear.

clue.text: Implausibly fast mover on yacht at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of on yacht are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something zips across the water impossibly quickly aboard a sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tachyon is a hypothetical particle travelling faster than light, so it is a theoretical speed demon.

clue.text: Arab country offloading Middle East currency

indicators.note: offloading means getting rid of the abbreviation for Middle East

parts.note: Yemen is an Arab country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: An Arab state is unloading its Middle Eastern cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The yen is the monetary unit of Japan.

clue.text: Instruments, black in appearance mostly

indicators.note: the black stuff goes inside the shortened word
mostly drops the last letter

parts.note: a guise is an outward appearance
tar is black pitch

explanation.surface: A rock band appears on stage with instruments that look mostly black.
explanation.definitionFit: Guitars are stringed musical instruments, the plural noun matching instruments.

clue.text: Cheat getting round a new rule

indicators.note: the cheat goes round the other pieces, surrounding them

parts.note: to con is to cheat or swindle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fraudster finds a way around a newly introduced regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a general law, principle or standard, as in the canons of good taste.

clue.text: Alpine lake falling short — unknown quantity needed for stability

indicators.note: falling short means the lake's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Lake Constance lies at the foot of the Alps between Germany, Austria and Switzerland
in algebra y is an unknown

explanation.surface: An Alpine lake's level drops and something unknown is needed to keep it steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Constancy is steadfastness and unchanging firmness, the quality of being stable.
